title: Common-precision centered tower and completed comparison interfaces
statement: For Elkik unions $(X,I),(Y,J)$ [def-per-elkik-pair-geometry] and ordinary ordered blowup towers $A$ on $X$ and $B$ on $Y$ [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule], the level diagram of $A_i$ is $V((I\mathcal O_{A_i})^t)$ with the restricted ordinary transition maps, structural maps, and center ideals. Its staggered level is the fibre at $n(n-i)$, its center is the restriction to that fibre, and its staggered arrow first includes the thinner fibre and then applies the ordinary transition; no off-center isomorphism is asserted. For a set of common orders $S\subset\mathbf N$ and base maps $h_t:Y_t\to X_t$, a comparison consists of one monotone contraction count and ordered embedding of retained centers, starting at zero and ending at the source length, incrementing at retained stages and remaining constant otherwise; maps from each repeated source level at $t$ to its target level; cartesian squares over $h_t$; commutation with every tower transition; equality of each retained center ideal with the extended target ideal; and deletion if and only if that extended ideal is the unit ideal. These level maps commute with the closed inclusions for all $s\le t$ in $S$. A finite comparison for $h:Y_m\to X_m$ through precision $T\le m$ includes its restrictions $h_t$, $1\le t\le T$, with equations over $h$, and that common-order comparison. A map of completed pairs is a natural transformation between the entire adic thickening diagrams [def-per-adic-formal-geometry] with equality of distinguished ideals at every order. Its actual formal ringed-space map is obtained by the colimit construction of that node; regularity is regularity on all complete formal affine section maps as in that node. A completed comparison is the comparison at all positive orders, with one contraction count and compatible level maps, hence preserves all completed center ideals. A completed-pair identification is an isomorphism of these diagrams preserving the distinguished ideals, with no field condition.
